entries.title: Fix: gymnast Personal Bests now credit full all-around totals from finals days
items: A gymnast's "Best All-Around" on the season-bests card used to ignore scores from Apparatus Finals or Day 2 rounds entirely, even when they competed a full all-around that day. If that finals-day total was their best of the season it was skipped and their second-best shown instead. Finals and Day 2 totals are now counted whenever the gymnast completed every apparatus that day, so a genuine best — for example a 56.625 all-around from the apparatus-finals day of a 2026 championship — ranks as the season's highest AA.
Partial finals-day sums (a gymnast who only did some of the apparatus) still don't count as an all-around.

entries.title: Fix: gymnast pages now reliably open on the current year
items: When opening a gymnast's page it's meant to default to the current season — but occasionally it could show every year's results at once, with the all-years view loading over the top of the selected year. The page now waits for the year list before loading results, and the shared results table drops out-of-order responses, so the year you pick (or the default year) is always the one you see.

entries.title: Fix: merged gymnast profiles no longer 404
items: When two duplicate profiles are merged from the Admin identity review, the old gymnast page URLs used to stop working (they had been bookmarked or shared, they'd show "Gymnast not found"). Old links — including any tabs opened before the merge — now automatically redirect to the surviving profile, whichever spelling or GNZ ID you had open.

entries.title: Fix: gymnast levels no longer picked up from unused result tables
items: A gymnast registered against extra competition tables they never scored in could be assigned the wrong level — for example a STEP 10 gymnast at CSG Classic 2026 was showing as Senior International because the source data listed Senior International tables first for her. Levels (and divisions) are now taken from the tables a gymnast actually has results in, so this class of data-entry mistake no longer corrupts rankings.

entries.title: SEO: pages are now search-engine friendly
items: Every public page now serves real content in the initial HTML (event names, gymnast and club profiles, counts) instead of a blank loading spinner — titles, meta descriptions, canonical URLs and Open Graph tags are generated per page.
Gymnast profile pages now appear in search results under the athlete's real name, and old /gymnast/{id} links automatically redirect to a readable address like /gymnast/a1b2c3d4e5-ewan-mcgregor.
Added a sitemap.xml covering every event, gymnast and club page, plus a robots.txt that keeps login and admin pages out of search results.
Event pages carry structured data (SportsEvent) and gymnast/club pages include Person/SportsOrganization markup so search engines can surface richer results.
Missing gymnasts, clubs and events now return a proper 404 instead of a page that looks fine to search engines but shows 'not found' only in the browser.

entries.title: Admin: Cloudflare traffic at a glance
items: The admin Graphs section now also shows the edge traffic Cloudflare sees for the site — total requests, bandwidth, unique visitors, blocked threats and cache-hit percentage over 7 or 30 days, plus per-day requests, response status codes and top visitor countries.
This covers everything the server-side dashboard can't see, like static assets and pages served through Cloudflare.

entries.title: Admin: everything on one page
items: All admin tools now live on a single Admin page — site stats and refresh on the left, the live usage dashboard (page views, API requests, errors, average response time) on the right, and all four usage graphs below spanning the full width.
Upload, Users, Identity Review and the logged-in activity log each open in a dialog from the buttons under the stats, keeping the dashboard clean.
The old separate /upload, /admin/activity and /admin/users pages are gone; the admin menu jumps straight to each tool.

entries.title: Admin: Activity page is now a usage dashboard
items: The admin Activity page now shows usage across the whole site, not just logged-in users — anonymous visitors and logged-in users are both counted (bots and scrapers are filtered out).

New graphs give an at-a-glance view: traffic over time, busiest hours of the day, most-viewed pages and most active users, plus totals for page views, API requests, errors and average response time — switch between 7 days, 30 days, 90 days or all time.
Page views from anonymous visitors are now recorded, and the dashboard works on mobile with the detail log collapsing into cards.

entries.title: Cleaner athlete identities on the live site
items: The live database was re-checked against the original event exports, and every gymnast's name spelling and GNZ ID was corrected to what the source results agree on.

Gymnasts that were accidentally lumped together now appear separately again — for example the two Simone Biles (at different clubs) are distinct athletes with their own pages, and over a thousand athletes had their correct ID restored.
Spelling variants (like McGregor/Mcgregor) are now consistently the most common form everywhere on the site.

entries.title: Two-day competitions show both days as separate rows
items: Results for multi-day meets (like Central Champs) now show each day as its own row with that day's apparatus scores and all-around mark — previously the two days were merged into a single row with the days' scores mixed together and the wrong all-around shown.
Each day keeps its correct apparatus scores, D-scores, ranks and all-around total (e.g. a gymnast's Day 1 41.900 and Day 2 43.516 now appear as two clean rows).

entries.title: Admin: one identity review to merge and split gymnasts
items: The admin dashboard's identity tools were merged into a single review that shows conflicts in both directions: similar-sounding names that may be one gymnast, the same name on multiple athletes, the same GNZ ID on multiple athletes, and one athlete carrying several IDs — each with the clubs, events and years as evidence.

Admins can now merge two athlete records into one (their results are combined under a single name and ID) or split one athlete that actually contains two people, moving selected rows into a new athlete. Splits stay in place across data rebuilds until explicitly merged.
The old 'Athlete ID Reconciliation' and 'Suggested Merges' cards were removed in favour of this view.

entries.title: One consistent spelling for every gymnast
items: All of a gymnast's results are now stored under a single spelling of their name — variants like 'Ewan Mcgregor' / 'Ewan McGregor', 'Newton-john' / 'Newton-John' and 'Suni' / 'Sunisa' Lee collapse to the most common form everywhere, including exports.
Gymnast totals and per-event competitor counts now count real people, so the homepage and event lists show exact numbers even when two athletes share a name (e.g. the two Simone Biles).

entries.title: One identity per gymnast
items: Every gymnast now has a stable identity that survives spelling differences and messy IDs — the gymnast list no longer shows duplicates like 'Ewan Mcgregor' and 'Ewan McGregor' as two people, and genuinely different athletes who share a name or ID (e.g. two Simone Biles) are kept apart.
Gymnast pages moved to stable links (e.g. /gymnast/a3f8b2c1d4) that don't break when an ID is corrected. Old gnz-id links still work.
Ranking tables, results tables and the Wellington rankings all group by the gymnast's identity, so spelling variants of the same person rank as one gymnast with their most common name.
Wellington intent tracking follows the gymnast identity too, so marking intent for a gymnast stays attached if their ID is ever corrected.

entries.title: Smarter athlete identity handling
items: Gymnast names keep their proper capitalization on import — names like McGregor, O'Neal and hyphenated surnames are no longer flattened to 'Mcgregor' or 'Neal'.

Importing a competition now checks for identity collisions: if two athletes share a name (e.g. two Simone Biles) or one ID appears on multiple names, the upload flags it as a warning instead of silently merging them.
ID reconciliation is safer: athletes who share a name but competed at the same event (or in different disciplines) are never auto-merged — they're reported for manual review in the admin dashboard.

An admin repair script (python -m app.repair_identities) can restore correct GNZ IDs and name spelling from the original event exports. It cross-checks every athlete against all source files, so a typo in one competition's data never overwrites a GNZ ID that the rest of the season agrees on.

entries.title: Reload prompt when a new version is deployed
items: If you leave the site open in a tab while an update is deployed, a banner now appears asking you to reload so you always see the latest results and features. Fresh page loads already pick up new versions automatically.

entries.title: Cleaner data for multi-day competitions
items: Did-Not-Start (DNS) entries are no longer stored as phantom score rows when a competition is imported — a gymnast who only competed one vault on a multi-day meet now shows a single real score instead of a DNS cell, and athletes who never competed at all no longer clutter the gymnast count.

entries.title: Rankings card on the homepage
items: Logged-in members now see a Rankings card on the homepage alongside Events, Results, Gymnasts and Clubs — a direct shortcut to the ranking pages.

entries.title: Mobile-friendly navigation and tables
items: The navigation bar no longer gets squashed on phones: the year filter is now a compact native selector (using your phone's own picker), the logo shrinks to an icon on small screens, and the theme menu fits any screen width. The mobile menu's brand header and icons were tidied up.

Result and ranking tables are easier to scan on a phone: the Rank and Name columns stay pinned together while you swipe sideways (on a gymnast page the competition name is pinned instead), low-value columns like GNZ ID are hidden on small screens, and the rank column is narrower.
Region columns use a compact colour-checker square on mobile with a tap-to-see tooltip for the region name (full badge on desktop), so score columns appear in the viewport sooner.

On phones and tablets, the club/region filters on the rankings pages and the column-header filters on results tables open as a full-width bottom sheet with larger tap targets, easy to use one-handed — pick your options and a Close button appears at the bottom of the sheet. The year, step and division selectors use your device's native picker.

The gymnast page's Personal Bests card, the Wellington tables and the Apparatus Qualifiers section all adapt cleanly to small screens, and 'not yet qualified' specialist badges use a dashed outline to look more temporary.
Filter popovers are clamped to the screen edge so they never run off the right side, and pagination controls wrap cleanly on narrow screens.

entries.title: Rankings filters: pick multiple clubs or regions
items: The Club and Region filters on the National and Apparatus Rankings pages now let you select more than one club or region at once — the menu stays open while you tick options.

Each funnel icon shows a count badge of how many clubs or regions are currently selected, so it's easy to see that a filter is applied. A Clear option sits at the bottom of each menu; choosing nothing shows everyone.

entries.title: Rankings filters stay applied when you change step or division
items: Club, Region and Over/Under selections are now kept when you switch step or division on the rankings pages instead of being reset.
If a selected club or region has no gymnasts in the new step it's dropped automatically so you never land on an empty table. Filters reset only when you change year or switch between WAG and MAG.

entries.title: Faster, more reliable rankings
items: The Apparatus Rankings page could take a very long time to load or get stuck on a spinner — two underlying causes were fixed.

Requests that carried a logged-in user's token each wrote an activity-log row to the database before the response was sent; under load these writes collided and stalled every request for seconds. Activity logging is now batched in the background, so a response never waits on it.
The apparatus ranking is now cached per year/step/division for 5 minutes and concurrent requests for the same view compute it once, so switching steps or reloading is near-instant.
A subtle rendering crash (duplicate gymnast IDs in the data) could leave the page frozen on the spinner even after the data arrived — the table no longer keys off the gymnast ID.

entries.title: Expired sessions sign you out cleanly instead of bouncing
items: If your login has expired (tokens last 7 days), the site now signs you out and takes you to the Login page when you visit a rankings or admin page — previously it could get stuck in a loop that looked like you had no access even though you did.
A hard refresh no longer gets stuck either, since an expired token is detected as soon as the page loads and is cleared from the browser.

entries.title: Fixed: missing apparatus scores on multi-day competitions
items: Results for multi-day competitions (like Central Champs) could show an athlete with only one or two apparatus scores while still displaying an all-around mark.

On the day an athlete didn't compete an apparatus, Scoreholder records a DNS pass; a DNS pass that landed as the first of two passes used to blank out the athlete's real score on that apparatus. It now correctly falls back to the scored pass, so every apparatus the athlete actually competed shows their mark.
Existing competitions are fixed automatically — no re-upload needed.

entries.title: New: Apparatus rankings
items: A new Apparatus Rankings page (under the Rankings menu, National access) shows who scored the highest on each apparatus in a step or level.
Pick a discipline, step and apparatus to see gymnasts ranked by their best single mark on that apparatus for the season, with the D-score and a tooltip showing the competition where the best was set.
Vault follows the same aggregation rules as the All Around ranking (e.g. STEP 6/7 average both vaults), and the Over/Under division filter works exactly like the national rankings.

entries.title: National rankings: apparatus qualifiers
items: STEP 8–10 (WAG) and Level 7+ (MAG) rankings now show an Apparatus Qualifiers section below the table — gymnasts who reached an apparatus qualifying mark but didn't qualify for the All Around ranking.

The qualifying marks match the Wellington rankings: 11.000 on the same apparatus at two different competitions for STEP 8–10, 11.500 on one apparatus for MAG Level 7+, and the per-apparatus specialist marks for Junior/Senior International.
Hover or focus any apparatus badge to see the competitions where the mark was reached; greyed-out badges show an apparatus where the mark has only been reached once so far.

The section appears alongside the 'Qualified' filter — turning it on filters the main table to qualifiers and lists the apparatus specialists below (gymnasts who already qualified for All Around are left out), and turning it off hides the section.
STEP 5 and above also get a callout at the top of the page explaining the ranking system, the qualifying marks, and what each toggle (Region Quotas, Qualified) does.
The Over/Under division filter is greyed out for STEP 9, STEP 10 and the international steps — those levels don't use division splits.

entries.title: Gymnast pages: season best summary
items: Picking a specific year on a gymnast's page now shows a Personal Bests card above the results table — the best score the gymnast achieved on each apparatus that season, with the D-score shown underneath, plus the best all-around they actually achieved.
Hover or focus any apparatus to see which competition and round the best score came from.
The card also sums the per-apparatus bests into a Best Possible AA score — the best score on each apparatus, combined.
The gymnast's GNZ ID, club, region and the step(s) they competed in that year are shown underneath their name when a specific year is selected.
A gymnast's page now defaults to the current year instead of All results (falls back to the most recent season with data if the current year isn't loaded yet).

entries.title: Fixed: phantom 2025 competitions
items: The Events timeline and table were showing a pile of identical competitions on 2 March 2025 — a batch of test Scoreholder exports had been imported more than once, leaving duplicate phantom events behind (each with almost no results).
All of those phantom March 2025 events have been removed entirely, along with one empty 2024 trial import that had no results.

Imports now replace every previous copy of the same competition (same name, date and discipline) instead of accumulating them, so this can't happen again — and a same-named event from a different year is left untouched.

entries.title: Season Timeline moves to the Events page
items: The season timeline now lives at the top of the Events page instead of a separate Timeline page — scroll the map, then the event table below it.
It appears only when a specific year is selected (desktop only); on the All-years view just the table shows, so the map and table always match.
Line and dot colours now adapt to light/dark themes.

entries.title: National rankings: Over/Under division filter
items: The National Rankings page (WAG) now has a Division dropdown next to the step selector — All Divisions, Over, or Under — so you can view a step's ranking split by over/under rather than combined.
The filter recomputes the ranking from only the selected division's competitions, so qualifier marks, the Q column, quota mode and exports all respect it.
The export filename/title appends 'Over' or 'Under' when a division is selected.

entries.title: Season Timeline
items: Every competition in a season drawn as a horizontally-scrollable map in the style of a London Underground diagram — theme-aware ink lines, consistent stroke widths and 45° elbows.
Each week with a competition gets a station dot on the main line, and each competition branches off to an inline station-style label with its date underneath.
Region colours appear as a 2×2 checkerboard marker on each branch (the same palette as the /clubs map); National Championships and events without a host club use a neutral grey marker.
Hover or focus any competition to see its full details (date, host club, region, WAG/MAG), and click to open its results.

entries.title: Medal counts for gymnasts, clubs and regions
items: Gold/silver/bronze totals now appear on the gymnast page, club page and gymnast list — tallied from every apparatus and all-around result the athlete placed in (1st/2nd/3rd).
Ties count as shared medals, and multi-pass vaults count once per event.
Every competition counts the same — National Championships and provincial team entries are tallied like any other meet.
Totals follow the year selector: pick a year to see that season's medals, or all years when none is selected.
In the result tables, every apparatus and all-around score that earned 1st/2nd/3rd now shows a gold, silver or bronze dot next to it.

entries.title: Bulk upload: club-dialog events no longer disappear
items: When importing multiple Scoreholder links and resolving unknown clubs with Save & Retry (or Keep all original), the imported event now stays visible in the upload list — previously it, and the rest of the batch's results, vanished from the list after the dialog, making it look like the event was never added.
Retry failures now also show as error cards instead of being silently hidden.

entries.title: National Rankings: filter by club or region
items: The Club and Region column headers now have a funnel icon that opens a filter — pick a club or a region (or both) to narrow the table instantly. Exports include the filtered rows, and the filter clears itself when you change year, step or discipline.

entries.title: National Rankings: STEP 1–4 qualifying indicator
items: STEP 1–4 now show a 'Q' column on the right of the table — a check means the gymnast has met the Gymnastics NZ qualifying score of 52.000 twice in the season (two different competitions), a dash means they haven't. Hovering the Q header shows what it means.

entries.title: National Rankings: table tidy-up
items: The Total column has been removed (the bolded Average remains), and the table shows two score columns for most steps and three for STEP 5/6.
The 'Enable Region Quotas' and 'Exclude non-qualifiers' toggles now have info tooltips explaining them, and both toggles are hidden for STEP 1–4 and MAG Level 1–3 where they don't apply.
When 'Exclude non-qualifiers' is on, a note appears below the table reminding you that the filter is hiding gymnasts who haven't reached the qualifying mark.
Score tooltips no longer get clipped at the right edge of the table.

entries.title: STEP 5/6 national rankings use the average of the top 3 scores
items: STEP 5 and STEP 6 rankings are now ordered by the average of each gymnast's three best competition scores (three score columns are shown). All other steps keep using the top two scores.

entries.title: Events page: host clubs shown in their region's colours
items: The Host Club column on the Events page now displays each host club in its region's colours (matching the region badges on the National Rankings), with long club names truncated.

entries.title: National Rankings: one mark per competition and corrected GNZ qualifying marks
items: Each gymnast now contributes only their highest mark from each competition, so a two-day meet (All Around + Apparatus Finals) can't fill both ranking slots.

The 'Exclude non-qualifiers' filter now uses the Gymnastics NZ qualifying rules: STEP 5/6 need two marks at 50.000 (one outside their home province), STEP 7–10 need two marks at 43.000 from different competitions, FIG Youth/Junior/Senior International need one mark at 42.500/43.000/45.000, and MAG Level 7–9, U18 and Senior Open need one mark at 63.000.

Events now have a Host Club that drives the STEP 5/6 'outside home province' rule (the club's region is used). It's guessed on upload and editable on the Events page; existing events can be filled in without re-uploading via 'python -m app.backfill_host_club' (dry-run first).

entries.title: What's new is now for logged-in users
items: The 'What's new' section on the homepage is now only shown to logged-in users.

entries.title: Wellington apparatus specialists: mark needed twice at different competitions
items: STEP 8–10 apparatus specialists now need to reach the qualifying mark (11.000) twice at different competitions on the same apparatus, instead of once on two different apparatus.

Athletes who have reached the mark only once so far on an apparatus get a greyed-out outline badge for that apparatus — alongside any solid badges for apparatus where the mark was reached twice or more. The ghost badge's tooltip notes the competition where the mark was reached and that a second competition is still needed.

entries.title: Rankings pages redirect signed-out visitors to the homepage
items: Visiting the National Rankings or Wellington Rankings pages without being logged in now redirects to the homepage instead of showing a load error. Members who don't have access to a particular ranking page are redirected too — for example, a member with National access only can't open the Wellington Rankings page.

entries.title: Admin pages redirect signed-out visitors to the homepage
items: Visiting /admin or /admin/users without being logged in now redirects to the homepage instead of showing an error-filled page. The redirect waits until the auth check resolves, so the admin UI never flashes.

entries.title: Login button now shows on every page
items: The site is now marked as in beta — the homepage shows an alert noting that results are provided as-is and may contain errors or inaccuracies, and the nav logo carries a small Beta badge.
Added a footer contact: found a bug? Email myles@hcg.org.nz.

entries.title: Login button now shows on every page
items: Fixed a bug where the Login button (and mobile menu's Login link) only appeared on the upload page — the auth-configured check was never run on other pages. It now appears in the nav across the site, including the homepage for signed-out visitors.

entries.title: Per-user page access for rankings
items: Admins can now grant or revoke access to each ranking page per user from the User Management page (National Rankings and Wellington Rankings checkboxes).
New members are granted National Rankings by default; Wellington Rankings access must be explicitly granted.
Users without access to a ranking page no longer see it in the nav menu, and visiting the page directly shows a "No access" message. Admins always have full access.

entries.title: Export buttons restyled
items: Export menus on all results and ranking tables now use the secondary theme colour and sit flush against the right edge of the toolbar.

entries.title: Wellington Rankings — presentation polish
items: Apparatus Specialists now appear above the "Not on the Ranking" table.
Team indicators are circles instead of badges, and the second-team (2) markers were removed for STEP 7+ levels — only the top-4 markers remain.
The step dropdown now lists STEP 5–10 then Youth, Junior, Senior in that order.

entries.title: International divisions on the Wellington Rankings
items: WAG Youth/Junior/Senior International levels now appear in the Wellington rankings step selector, ranked by a gymnast's single highest All Around mark.
Gymnastics NZ qualifying marks on one occasion: Youth 42.500, Junior 43.000, Senior 45.000.

Junior and Senior International athletes can also qualify as apparatus specialists by reaching the mark on one apparatus (Junior: VT 12.200 / UB 10.400 / BB 10.500 / FX 11.400; Senior: VT 12.500 / UB 11.300 / BB 11.200 / FX 11.400) — vault is the average of two.
MAG Level 7+ now also lists apparatus specialists who reach 11.500 on one apparatus.

entries.title: Wellington Rankings — combined "Not on the Ranking" table
items: The separate "In Progress" and "Not on the Ranking" tables are merged into one, listed alphabetically: every Wellington athlete who isn't on the ranking.

Each row's tooltip shows a check/cross requirements checklist — regional, named and away events, intent, and the GNZ/Wellington qualifying marks — each showing what's achieved and what's still missing (e.g. "2 away competitions (1 of 2)").

The ranking now always shows only qualified and intended athletes (the GNZ/Wellington/Intent filter toggles are gone); everyone else appears below, and ticking an athlete's Intent moves them up immediately.

Score columns in the lower table now align with their category slots (Regional Best / Next Best / Away Best) — each event appears in the right column, with a dash where an athlete has no event for that slot.

entries.title: Accessibility pass — all pages 100/100 on Lighthouse
items: Keyboard access everywhere: mobile menu, file upload, table sorting and filters, score/competition tooltips, the NZ region map, and every dialog.
Dialogs now trap focus, close on Escape, and restore focus to the button that opened them.
Screen-reader labels added to all inputs, selects, icon-only buttons, toasts, and error messages; navigation announces the current page.
Reduced-motion preference is respected by the landing-page animations.
Contrast fixes across light and dark themes, including the club region badges and the map focus indicator.

entries.title: Home, clubs & NZ map polish
items: Landing page: the three info items (WAG & MAG, Export & Share, Smart Filtering) moved above the clickable nav cards and stripped of card styling, so the links clearly read as links.
Wellington Rankings: removed the coloured top border on the qualification-protocol card.
NZ map: hovering or selecting a region sets its checker pattern scrolling diagonally — each region has its own direction and speed.
Clubs page on mobile: the map is replaced by a collapsible accordion of the region cards (tap to expand), listed north to south.

entries.title: Gymnast browsing upgrades
items: Gymnasts page: sticky header with the search box and alphabet jump bar inline, so both stay visible while scrolling.
The alphabet bar highlights the section you're currently viewing, and a 'Back to top' button appears once you scroll.
Home-page stat badges and Wellington apparatus-specialist badges now use the default text style (no monospace).
Events list: the 'Nationals' badge now sits next to the event name in accent styling instead of the Discipline column.

entries.title: Full update history on the landing page
items: 'What's new' now shows the entire patch-note history in a scrollable section instead of only the latest few entries.

entries.title: Export to CSV, XLSX & PDF
items: One dropdown on every results and rankings page — download CSV, Excel, or a printable PDF.
XLSX keeps full per-pass detail with tidy column widths; PDF mirrors the on-screen table with a header and page numbers.

entries.title: Interactive NZ map for clubs
items: Explore clubs on a clickable map of 15 gymnastics regions with theme colours and smooth panel transitions.
Provincial teams sit next to their region header, separate from regular clubs.

entries.title: Smarter uploads from URLs
items: Paste a Scoreholder event link to import it directly — no need to download and upload the JSON file.
Unknown clubs are flagged with suggested mappings (exact + fuzzy matches) you can accept or keep as-is.

entries.title: Landing page remix
items: Live stat counts now sit as badges on each nav card; the separate stats row is gone.
Added a 'What's new' section fed from patch notes, with a subtle on-load reveal that respects reduced-motion.

entries.title: Wellington rankings: intent tracking & team badges
items: Admins can mark which gymnasts intend to compete at Wellington events; a filter shows only those athletes.
Top-4 (1st Team) and 5–8 (2nd Team) badges highlight the strongest WAG STEP 7+ athletes.
Qualifier warning tooltips explain why an athlete did or didn't qualify.
Apparatus specialists (WAG STEP 8–10) who hit the qualifying mark on two apparatus now appear with colour-coded badges and competition tooltips.

entries.title: Inline editing in results tables
items: Admins can fix a gymnast's name, GNZ ID, or club right in the results table with a per-row save.

entries.title: WAG STEP 7–10 qualification tightened
items: Now requires two GNZ-qualifying scores from different competitions (was a single score).
MAG Level 7+ Wellington qualifying threshold set to 63.0.

entries.title: Admin cache refresh
items: New Refresh Cache button on the admin dashboard instantly clears the backend cache after uploads or edits.
Ranking endpoints no longer browser-cached so intent and qualifier toggles reflect immediately.

entries.title: Wellington regional rankings
items: Regional rankings for WAG STEP 5–6 and 7–10 with GNZ + Wellington dual-qualifier filters.
Distinct-event enforcement, per-step-range selection rules, and a dedicated rankings page with WAG/MAG tabs.

entries.title: Faster pages
items: Backend caching refactored with per-key TTLs and per-event invalidation; database indexes and SQLite PRAGMA tuning.
Optimised HTTP Cache-Control headers (public + stale-while-revalidate on reads, no-store on writes).
Pagination and debounced search in the results table.

entries.title: Browsing polish
items: Gymnasts page gains letter-jump navigation, live search, and tidier name/ID/club layout.
Visual hierarchy improvements, new scoreboard logo/favicon, and regional colour differentiation.

entries.title: National season rankings
items: Season rankings per discipline and STEP: best 2 competitions per gymnast (Nationals excluded), summed total, ties marked 'T'.
Region quota and qualifier filters let you focus on qualifying marks.
Gymnasts with only partial apparatus passes get a computed All-Around aggregate.

entries.title: Nationals flag on events
items: Admins can mark an event as a Nationals competition, which excludes it from season rankings.

entries.title: Athlete ID reconciliation & duplicate resolution
items: Admin dashboard groups athletes by name with per-instance GNZ ID dropdowns and confidence-based auto-fix.
Suggested merges detect similar names (e.g. nicknames/spelling variants) with one-click merge.

entries.title: Region badges & colours
items: Each of the 15 gymnastics regions gets its own NZ-sports-inspired colour palette and a checkerboard badge.
Region column added to wide results tables (enriched from club lookup, filterable).

entries.title: Cleaner names & production deployment
items: Automatic name cleanup at import: diacritics normalised, trailing (L#) / (STEP 10) / (YI) suffixes stripped, metadata removed.
Production Docker Compose with multi-stage frontend build and /api proxying through the frontend server.

entries.title: Accounts & role-based access
items: Username + password login with JWT tokens and admin/member roles.
Admin user management (create accounts, reset passwords, delete).
Upload, Admin, and Rankings links are gated by role.
Global year selector in the nav bar applied across all data pages.

entries.title: Club mapping on upload
items: When a file references a club we don't recognise, a dialog lets you map it to a known club or keep the original name.
Round-type parsing fixed: 'Qualification' suffix stripped, Day 2 classified correctly, individual scores skipped in All-around PRTs.

entries.title: Multi-file upload & faster results
items: Drag-and-drop supports multiple files with a per-file status queue.
In-memory cache for wide pivots plus Cache-Control/ETag headers on read endpoints.
CSV/XLSX exports include per-pass vault and bonus columns.

entries.title: Division & round fixes
items: Division falls back to the unit name when the level is missing; GfA levels filtered out.
Day 2 round-type collision fixed; discipline derived from apparatus in competition node trees.

entries.title: Gymnast & club browsing
items: New gymnasts list page (searchable, grouped A–Z) and clubs list page grouped by region.
Year selectors on gymnast and club result pages; stats cards link through to events, results, and clubs.

entries.title: Upload, events, and protected writes
items: Landing page redesigned; upload moved to its own page.
Event search, sortable columns, delete, and rename.
Password-based auth with a login page protecting write routes.
Filtered CSV export on the event detail page (exports only the currently filtered rows).

entries.title: Wide results, tooltips, and export expansion
items: Tailwind + DaisyUI restyle with dark theme and a sticky nav.
Per-apparatus score tooltips (D/E/N/bonus/rank) and an All-Around tooltip.
Per-pass vault columns with level-aware aggregation (STEP 6/7 average, high-level best/avg).
WAG/MAG tabs split results by discipline; DNS/DNF handled; bonus propagated across passes.
All-results view across every event.

entries.title: NZ Gymnastics Results launches
items: Backend parses Scoreholder JSON exports into a normalised SQLite database.
FastAPI endpoints for upload, events, results, and CSV/XLSX export.
SvelteKit frontend with a drag-and-drop upload page and events/results browsing.
Docker Compose for easy local development.
